title: Cauliflower Pilaf
description: My Thermomix take on Ravinder Bhogal's fragrant cauliflower pilaf — golden, spiced rice with tender cauliflower florets, toasted cashews and fresh herbs, all cooked in one bowl.
intro: This is my independent Thermomix homage to Ravinder Bhogal and the warming appeal of a good cauliflower pilaf. It keeps the spirit of the original inspiration — fragrant spices hugging tender cauliflower through golden rice — but the method is written fresh for TM6 and TM7 cooks who want clear settings and a comforting, achievable result.
ingredients: 300 g basmati rice, rinsed and soaked 20 min
1 small cauliflower (approx. 500 g), cut into small florets
steps: Place onion, garlic and ginger in the mixing bowl. Chop 5 sec / speed 7, then scrape down the sides.
Add ghee or oil. Sauté 3 min / 120°C / speed 1, MC off, until the onion is soft and fragrant.
Add cumin seeds, turmeric, garam masala and chilli flakes. Toast 1 min / 120°C / speed 1, MC off, until the spices bloom.

Drain the soaked rice well. Add rice to the mixing bowl along with the cauliflower florets, water and salt. Cook 18 min / 100°C / Reverse / speed 1, MC on, until the rice is tender and the cauliflower is soft.
Meanwhile, place cashews in a dry small frying pan and toast over medium heat on the stovetop until golden, about 3 min, shaking often. Set aside.
Once cooked, rest the pilaf in the bowl 2 min / 0°C / Reverse / speed 0 so the grains firm up and excess moisture absorbs.
Fluff gently with the spatula, stir through the lemon juice, then transfer to a warm serving platter. Scatter the toasted cashews, coriander and mint over the top and serve immediately.
tips: Don't skip soaking the rice — it gives you fluffier, separate grains and reduces cook time.
Swap cashews for toasted almonds or pistachios if you prefer.
This keeps well refrigerated for 2 days and reheats beautifully with a splash of water.

faq.q: Can I use cauliflower rice instead of florets?
faq.a: You can, but add it in the last 5 minutes of cooking so it doesn't turn to mush. Florets hold their shape better in a pilaf.

faq.q: Is this the original Ravinder Bhogal recipe?
faq.a: No. This is Chef Aly's independent Thermomix reinterpretation inspired by Ravinder Bhogal and cauliflower pilaf; it is not endorsed by or affiliated with the chef.
